title: Let's go Bananas with GenMedia — Guillaume Vernade, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A Google DeepMind developer advocate demos Gemini's generative-media models (Nano Banana images, Veo video, Lyria music, TTS) by illustrating a public-domain book, showing prompt-chaining tricks and API features like service tiers and stateful interactions. It is a product/API demo, not an agent-engineering talk, but a few cost and context mechanisms are copyable.

takeaways.technique: Service tiers (flex vs priority) per request
takeaways.what_they_do: Same model offered at three tiers: normal queue, 'flex' at 50% discount with multi-minute delay tolerance, and 'priority' at 2x price for guaranteed fast track; caller picks per request.

takeaways.technique: Stateful interaction IDs instead of resending history
takeaways.what_they_do: New API returns an interaction ID; subsequent calls reference it so the server restores context, avoiding re-uploading the full prompt every turn, and it auto-caches for cheaper reuse.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need to re-upload the same context again and again and again at every turn of the conversation

takeaways.technique: Structured output to drive downstream steps
takeaways.what_they_do: Uses JSON-schema structured output to get chapter name, prompt, and the list of characters present, then feeds only the matching reference images to the next generation call instead of relying on chat history.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the name of the chapter, the prompt, but also the list of the characters that are appearing in this chapter

takeaways.technique: Separate prompt-generation step before the expensive call
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of reusing the image prompt for video, a cheap Gemini call writes a dedicated video prompt describing what happens next; this fixed wrong-character/wrong-action outputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: asking Gemini to come up with a new um a new prompt just for the just for the video and to explain what's what's happening afterwards

takeaways.technique: Client-side auto-retry with backoff on overload
takeaways.what_they_do: Wraps the client with automatic retry (5 attempts, 2s apart) because models get overloaded at peak times.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's going to be automatically retrying five times after 2 secs

takeaways.what_they_do: Iterate prompts on the cheapest video model (5c/sec) and only upscale to the expensive model once the prompt is right.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the idea is that you can iterate on um on on the prompt that way and then upscale afterwards
takeaways.numbers: ~40 cents per cheap video vs premium model
